source.paraphrase: An external call has a bounded timeout or deadline. An indefinite wait is a failure.

invariants.why: A network call with no deadline can hang the request until the process is killed.
invariants.fixHint: Pass an AbortSignal with a timeout, or the client's timeout option, and decide what the caller does when it fires.
invariants.avoid: Putting signal: null in the options still contains the word signal and is a hole. A headers bag is not a deadline.

relations.why: A .query() call with an interpolated template literal is reported by both rules.
relations.settle: Keep both: a parameterized query ($1 placeholders with a values array) satisfies both, and PG-CONCAT-001 also catches + concatenation.

relations.why: Prisma.raw(`...${value}`) is a raw method with an interpolated first argument, so both rules report it.
relations.settle: Keep both. A $queryRaw tagged template or Prisma.sql satisfies both; PRISMA-RAW-002 also catches + concatenation.

source.paraphrase: Queries go to the database through parameters. String concatenation and interpolation of SQL are not a query API.

invariants.why: A value spliced into SQL is an injection point. The database sees the caller's text as syntax.
invariants.fixHint: Pass the SQL text with placeholders and send values as a separate argument list.
invariants.avoid: This syntax check inspects a directly interpolated first argument of a query, execute, raw or unsafe method. Scope strings in other arguments and outer callbacks are not SQL. A $1 placeholder passes. Variables, concatenations and tagged sql templates require separate review; this rule does not prove their data flow or parameterization.

source.paraphrase: Production CORS is not Access-Control-Allow-Origin * together with credentials.

invariants.why: A credentialed request reflected to every origin lets any site call the API with the user's cookies.
invariants.fixHint: List the origins that may send credentials. A public API that needs no cookies can use * only without credentials.
invariants.avoid: Splitting the two fields across lines does not split the object. A star origin without credentials is a different policy and is allowed here.

source.paraphrase: Writes bind an allowlist of client fields. Spreading the raw request body into a create or update lets the caller set any column.

invariants.why: The body can carry role, price, or owner. Writing it through copies those fields into the row.
invariants.fixHint: Pick the fields this operation accepts and pass only those.
invariants.avoid: Aliasing the body to a local and then spreading the local is a hole. Spreading request.body under another name in the same call is still the raw body.

source.paraphrase: HTML from a caller is encoded or sanitized. A raw HTML injection prop is a sink.

invariants.why: The prop inserts markup. A string that passed through a user becomes script in the page.
invariants.fixHint: Render text as text. If a subset of HTML is required, sanitize it in one named function and keep that function the only caller.
invariants.avoid: Renaming a wrapper that still passes the prop through does not remove the prop. The name is the sink.

source.work: vibe-proof auditor checklist; MDN Web Docs, Element: innerHTML property
source.paraphrase: HTML from a caller is encoded or sanitized. Setting innerHTML to a string you do not control is a cross-site scripting vector; use textContent for plain text.

invariants.why: innerHTML, outerHTML, insertAdjacentHTML and document.write parse their string as markup, so a value that passed through a user becomes script in the page.
invariants.fixHint: Set textContent or build elements with createElement. If a subset of HTML is required, sanitize it in one named function and keep that function the only writer.
invariants.avoid: Bracket access such as el["outerHTML"], += appends and template literals with ${} are the same sink. String literals, templates without ${} and ternaries of them are allowed, as is reading innerHTML.

source.locator: Error handling, stack traces not exposed
source.paraphrase: End users do not receive stack traces. Diagnostic detail stays in server logs.

invariants.why: A stack trace shows file paths, dependency versions, and sometimes query text to the caller.
invariants.fixHint: Send a stable message and a correlation id. Log the stack on the server.
invariants.avoid: err["stack"] is the same property. logger.error(error.stack) is not a response and is not this rule.

source.paraphrase: Entry points validate input on the server. A body that is used raw skipped that step.

invariants.why: The JSON body is untyped input. Using it without a parser lets a missing field or an extra field through as if it were an invoice.
invariants.fixHint: Parse the JSON with a schema's safeParse and branch on the failure before the value reaches a write.
invariants.avoid: A comment that says safeParse is not a call. A local function that is also named safeParse and does nothing is a hole: the call exists and the schema does not.
